Users need a Figma Weave account connected to their Figma account to generate media mid-conversation. Each video or image generated with a Weave model consumes Weave credits.
articles.one-liner: Figma now enables external AI agents to trigger media generation models like Kling and Seedance directly within workflows via the Figma MCP.

summary.what: Figma integrated its Weave video and image models into the Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing third-party agents to generate assets. It also added version control for generative plugins, enabling developers to restore previous iterations.
summary.why: By connecting generative models to MCP, Figma is positioning itself as a foundational platform layer for agentic workflows rather than just a design tool.
summary.takeaway: If you are building AI agents, you can now access Figma's media models via the Figma MCP by linking your Figma Weave account.

articles.deep-summary:
* **MCP Integration**: Allows cross-platform AI agents to trigger Figma's video and image generation models.
* **Version Control**: Every change to a generative plugin or shader now creates an agent-annotated change log.
* **Credits**: Media generation is metered via Weave credits, requiring an active account.
articles.decoder:
* **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**: An open-source standard created by Anthropic that allows AI models to connect securely to external data sources and tools.
* **Weave**: Figma's internal suite of generative AI tools and infrastructure for design and prototyping.

articles.title: 3 design principles in the AI age
articles.description: Three enduring principles remain essential to good design despite AI dramatically accelerating creative work: iteration, feedback, and connecting the dots. Faster generation makes exploring alternatives cheaper, but quality still requires repeated refinement, diverse human perspectives, and judgment about which feedback matters rather than accepting AI's first answer or treating it as the only critic. Designers also need time away from production to process accumulated knowledge and recognize larger connections, because AI can generate faster than humans can meaningfully reflect.
articles.one-liner: AI acceleration makes creative generation cheaper, but high-quality design remains rooted in the human-led processes of iteration, feedback, and reflection.

summary.what: Experts argue that designers must guard against 'AI-first' complacency. Essential principles like iteration, diverse feedback loops, and periods of cognitive reflection are more critical as AI increases the sheer volume of output.
summary.why: This marks a shift in the design industry's maturity phase where the novelty of AI generation is being replaced by the necessity of refined human judgment and strategic thinking.

articles.title: Design as a garden
articles.description: Creative work can be approached like tending a garden: cultivate favorable conditions, return consistently, encourage unexpected cross-pollination, and protect fragile ideas before judging them too quickly. Pruning unnecessary work and deliberately leaving room for play can be as important as producing more, while not every experiment needs an obvious payoff. Ideas also benefit from periods of inactivity and patience, making it useful to distinguish between moments that require greater effort and those that simply require more time.
articles.one-liner: Creative work should be managed like a garden, emphasizing patience, the protection of fragile ideas, and the importance of fallow periods.

summary.what: Designer Justin Wang advocates for a 'gardening' approach to productivity, advising practitioners to prune non-essential tasks, avoid premature judgment of ideas, and embrace periods of inactivity for mental renewal.

articles.title: Accessible Components Library (Website)
articles.description: Accessible components with working examples, code, guidance, and the test scenarios to check them.
articles.one-liner: Tetralogical has published a library of accessible UI components including Gherkin-based test scenarios to verify WCAG 2.2 compliance.

summary.what: The library provides code examples and accessibility documentation for common UI components. Each component includes test scenarios written in Gherkin to standardize how developers check for WCAG compliance.
summary.why: This offers a practical bridge between abstract accessibility guidelines and concrete code, helping teams treat accessibility as an automated, testable requirement.
summary.takeaway: Use the Gherkin scenarios provided in the repo to integrate accessibility regression testing into your existing test suites.

articles.deep-summary:
* **Gherkin Formatting**: Uses plain-language syntax (Given/When/Then) to define accessibility tests.
* **Scope**: Includes documentation for input assistance, keyboard navigation, and reflow.
* **License**: Released under the ISC license for free reuse.
articles.decoder:
* **WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines)**: A set of international standards for making web content more accessible to people with disabilities.
* **Gherkin**: A business-readable language used for behavior-driven development (BDD) to define test cases in plain text.

articles.title: AI CAD Generator for Structured Parametric Models (Website)
articles.description: Turn engineering intent into structured CAD with zCAD AI. Describe requirements, generate the model, inspect the result, and continue through revision.
articles.one-liner: zCAD AI is a new tool that generates structured, parametric CAD models from natural language descriptions for non-commercial users.

summary.what: The platform offers a browser-based interface where users provide engineering requirements to generate 3D models. It supports standard export formats including STEP and allows for iterative revisions, currently capped at 200 credits per month on the free tier.

articles.decoder: * **Parametric model**: A 3D CAD design defined by variables and constraints, allowing for automated updates to dimensions or features without redrawing the entire model.

articles.title: Microsoft's identity for Copilot positions it as a tool for work
articles.description: Microsoft's evolving Copilot identity positions AI as a practical tool embedded in everyday work rather than an abstract futuristic technology. Its animated two-part mark, paired sans-serif and serif typography, gradients, and flexible graphic system create continuity across Microsoft's ecosystem while giving Copilot a recognizable presence of its own. The system is designed to scale across product interfaces, campaigns, and motion, balancing the expressiveness needed to represent generative AI with the clarity expected from a productivity tool.
articles.one-liner: Microsoft is rebranding Copilot with a flexible, productivity-focused visual identity to ground generative AI as a reliable workplace utility.

summary.what: Microsoft implemented a new two-part mark, specific typography pairings, and a gradient system to unify the Copilot brand across its ecosystem, moving away from futuristic, abstract branding toward a functional tool aesthetic.
summary.why: This shift highlights the industry trend of stabilizing AI marketing by emphasizing integration into familiar workflows rather than highlighting the novelty of the underlying technology.

articles.title: Nine Checks Before Shipping a Product Email: A Workflow for Developers and Designers
articles.description: A product email can look right in a design file yet fail its reader through a vanishing action, a surviving staging link, or a duplicate send. Using a workspace invitation as the example, nine checks cover the message's behavioral contract, client compatibility, accessibility, captured application output, link validation, and retry handling. Delivery evidence, such as authentication and bounce handling, is reviewed separately after the template passes.
articles.one-liner: A rigorous pre-send checklist for product emails can prevent common failures like broken staging links or missing action buttons.

summary.what: The workflow suggests nine validation steps before deployment, including checking behavioral contracts, client-side rendering compatibility, accessibility standards, link integrity, and retry logic handling for failed sends.
summary.takeaway: Adopt a mandatory pre-send checklist covering client rendering tests and link validation to avoid critical errors in automated user communications.

articles.deep-summary:
* Behavioral contract: Confirming the email triggers based on intended user actions.
* Client compatibility: Testing how emails render across major providers like Gmail, Outlook, and Apple Mail.
* Accessibility: Verifying screen reader compatibility and sufficient color contrast.
* Output validation: Ensuring dynamic data placeholders pull correct user-specific information.
* Link validation: Checking all destination URLs for staging environment remnants.
* Delivery evidence: Reviewing SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication settings.
* Bounce handling: Confirming the system is configured to capture and process failed delivery reports.
articles.decoder: * **Behavioral contract**: The defined set of conditions and expected outcomes for an automated interaction, such as sending an email only after a specific user action.

articles.title: Estonian Street Artist is Transforming Ordinary City Walls into Bizarre, Cartoonish Masterpieces
articles.description: Estonian designer and street artist Ingmar Järve, known as Gutface, fills murals, prints, and digital work with distorted figures, deadpan faces, and satirical cartoon humor.
articles.one-liner: Estonian artist Ingmar Järve, known as Gutface, creates satirical, distorted murals that merge raw street art with clean graphic design.

summary.what: Järve produces large-scale murals and digital illustrations featuring deadpan faces and surreal motifs to provide cynical commentary on modern urban life.

articles.title: Apple exploring fix for Safari's cramped layout on the iPhone Duo's outer display
articles.description: Apple is exploring ways for websites to extend into the space behind Safari's right-aligned controls on the iPhone Duo's outer display, potentially giving web designers more usable width without obscuring important content.
articles.one-liner: Apple is investigating ways to let websites utilize space behind Safari's UI elements on the iPhone Duo's dual-screen form factor.

summary.what: Apple is exploring software-level adjustments to Safari's interface on the iPhone Duo, aimed at preventing the right-aligned control bars from obscuring website content on the outer display.

articles.title: How Do You Create a Design to Last for 1,000 Years?
articles.description: Nebbia's Interlude, a climbable stone portal on a cliff overlooking Lake Whakatipu, is the second completed work in Paererewā's plan for 1,000 works lasting 1,000 years.
articles.one-liner: London studio Nebbia designed a basalt stone portal in New Zealand as part of a 1,000-year project focused on geological rather than human-centric time.

summary.what: The 'Interlude' sculpture, commissioned by the Paererewā initiative, uses locally sourced basalt bluestone designed to potentially erode or fragment over centuries, prioritizing ecological longevity over static preservation.
